title: Suggested hobbies and activities lists
description: This latent fires on list items and questions that enumerate hobbies, leisure activities, or self-improvement suggestions (e.g., 'hiking, reading, playing video games', 'try yoga, meditation, or journaling', 'are you into sports, music, or gaming?'), typically in advice-giving contexts about finding interests, coping strategies, or bonding topics. It also activates on the numbered/bulleted list markers ('2.', '3. **', '4.') that structure these suggestion lists, since these tokens co-occur tightly with the hobby-enumeration pattern. It does not activate on general advice about relationships, emotional support, or communication strategies that lack an explicit list of activities/hobbies, nor on narrative or explanatory sentences even if they discuss personal growth abstractly rather than listing concrete activity options.

title: Preemptive warning / expectation management
description: This latent activates on sentences describing someone having previously warned or cautioned another party and/or actively managing expectations about an anticipated outcome or reaction. It responds to narrative descriptions of forewarning behavior paired with efforts to soften, prepare for, or control how someone will respond to news or events. It would not activate on simple factual statements, direct warnings issued in the moment (e.g., 'Watch out!'), or descriptions of reactions themselves without reference to prior forewarning or expectation-setting. The key trigger is the combination of retrospective warning ('had warned') plus proactive expectation management ('trying to manage expectations'), not warnings or reactions in isolation.

title: Empathetic conversational opener
description: This latent fires on short, formulaic empathetic or acknowledging exclamations that an assistant uses to open a response to a personal/advice-seeking query, e.g. 'I totally get it!', 'What a tricky situation!', 'I'm here to help!', 'dilemma!'. It activates most strongly on these stock phatic phrases that signal understanding, validation, or willingness to help before substantive content is given, and more weakly on surrounding text that continues to frame the response as navigating a difficult personal situation. It does not activate on the substantive advice content itself (specific recommendations, analysis of who is at fault, concrete suggestions), nor on plain factual or narrative sentences that lack this empathetic/acknowledging framing tone, even if they discuss similarly emotional or dilemma-laden topics.

title: Advice list item openers
description: This latent fires on the very first token(s) of an item in an advice or suggestion list: imperative verb starters like 'Be', 'Try to', 'Remember to', 'Consider', 'Practice', or gerund/preposition openers like 'By', as well as bare numeral list markers ('2.', '3.', '4.', '5.') that introduce a new bullet in a numbered list of recommendations. It activates most strongly on these short fragmentary openers themselves, and more weakly on fuller sentences that still begin with such an imperative or 'By ...' construction (e.g. 'Be patient, communicate openly', 'By focusing...'). It does not activate on descriptive, narrative, or explanatory sentences that lack this list-item/imperative opening structure, such as statements of fact, questions, or mid-sentence continuations, even if they occur within the same advice-giving passage.

title: Numbered list item markers
description: This latent fires on the numeral or bullet marker that begins an enumerated list item, such as a standalone digit like '2.', '3', '4.', etc., often followed by bold header text or a colon. It activates most strongly on bare number tokens marking list positions, and more weakly on sentences that are themselves list-item content within advice or step-by-step responses (e.g., 'Respect his boundaries**: ...'). It would not activate on ordinary prose sentences lacking list structure, nor on numbers used as quantities or dates within a sentence rather than as item markers.
